contracts_changed: Manifest capability states other than supported require an explanatory reason in both Rust registration validation and the Python metadata validator.
Capability requires entries are unique, non-empty strings.
Python metadata validation uses the v1 manifest, schema, defaults, package source, and common SemVer range subset without importing component code.
implemented: Added a dependency-free Python metadata validator for component IDs, API/schema versions, kinds, entry points, nested parameter Schema/defaults, capabilities, dependency declarations, package source fingerprints, and basic parameter values.
Aligned Rust capability validation with Python: unsupported/unknown/conditional states require reasons even when written as scalar strings, and requires entries must be unique and non-empty.

Added Rust integration coverage using shared valid/invalid metadata examples; verifies Rust registration accepts nested defaults/capabilities and rejects unexplained capabilities and malformed dependency ranges.
Added direct Python validator coverage for accepted nested schema/defaults and rejection of unsupported capabilities, invalid defaults, and malformed dependency ranges.

Coordinator integrated validate_manifest into the static discovery path before component registration and embedded extensions/metadata.py. Invalid manifest metadata becomes a per-entry discovery issue; the import-marker integration regression confirms discovery remains static.
